question: I changed jobs and want to log in with my new address. How do I change my account email, and will invoices go there too?
reference_answer: In Account settings > Security, enter your current password and new email in the Email Address area and confirm with the code sent to the new address. That only changes your Plausible login email: invoices go to the separate Paddle email, which is changed another way.
key_facts: Change it in Security > Email Address with password and verification code
Verification code is sent to the new email
Invoices go to the Paddle email, which this doesn't change
answer: To change your Plausible login email, go to your account settings, navigate to the Security section, provide your current password and new email, and click the Change Email button [1]. You will then need to provide a verification code sent to your new address [1]. Please note that your Plausible login email and your Paddle invoice email are separate [2][1]. Changing your login email does not automatically update your invoice email [1]. If you would like invoices sent to a different address, please contact us with your current Paddle email and the new address you would like to use [3].

Note that our system has two email addresses and that these may not necessarily be the same. One is for your Plausible account and the other one for your Paddle account.

## Give your accounting team billing access

You can add a team member with the Billing role. A Billing member can view all past invoices, save them as PDFs and manage your subscription and payment details directly within Plausible.

To add a billing member, go to your team settings and invite them with the Billing role. See users and roles for details.

question: My dashboard lists macOS 10.15 for most of my Mac visitors even though I know many have newer versions. Why is that?
reference_answer: Windows and macOS have stopped reporting their latest versions, so Plausible and other analytics tools can't report them. Visitors with newer versions, above 10 for Windows and above 10.15 for macOS, are grouped under the last known version.
key_facts: Windows and macOS no longer report their latest versions
Newer versions are grouped under the last known version (macOS 10.15, Windows 10)
answer: Windows and macOS have stopped reporting their latest versions [1]. This means that Plausible and other analytics tools are not able to report the latest versions, which for macOS are above 10.15 [1]. Visitors with the new versions will be grouped in the last known version [1].

question: I want to test my new signup goal without polluting the real numbers. Can I delete the test conversions afterwards?
reference_answer: No, conversions can't be deleted for a single goal, because a goal shows events Plausible has already recorded. Instead, test with a temporary event name such as `Signup test` and switch to the real name once it works, or test on a separate staging site added to Plausible.
key_facts: Conversions can't be deleted for a single goal
Test with a temporary event name, then change to the real name
Alternatively test on a separate site
answer: Conversions cannot be deleted for a single goal [1][2]. To keep test clicks out of your data, you can test with a temporary event name and change it to the real name once you confirm it works [1]. Alternatively, you can add your staging site as a separate site in Plausible to run tests before setting up the goal on your live site [1].

citations.quote: Conversions can't be deleted for a single goal.
Test with a temporary event name. Send the event as `Signup test` while you check that it fires. Once it works, change your code to the real name, such as `Signup`, and edit the goal to use it.
Test on a separate site. Add your staging site to Plausible as its own site and run your tests there before you set up the goal on your live site.
Stats for a single page, a single goal or specific custom property values can't be deleted on their own once they've been recorded.

evidence.title: Goal conversions
evidence.text:
A goal doesn't store data of its own. It shows the events Plausible has already recorded, so removing a goal and adding it again brings back every conversion it showed before. Conversions can't be deleted for a single goal. Resetting your stats clears the stats for the whole site from your dashboard.

To keep your test clicks out of a new custom event goal:

* **Test with a temporary event name.** Send the event as `Signup test` while you check that it fires. Once it works, change your code to the real name, such as `Signup`, and edit the goal to use it. Your test conversions stay with the old name and don't show in the goal.
* **Test on a separate site.** Add your staging site to Plausible as its own site and run your tests there before you set up the goal on your live site.

Pageview goals work without code changes, so there's usually nothing to test. Exclude your own visits if you don't want to count yourself when you check the page.

evidence.title: Reset your site data
evidence.text:
Within the **Danger zone** section of your website settings, find **Reset stats** and click **Reset [your domain] stats**. Confirm the reset when prompted.

Plausible site settings: Reset stats clears collected stats from the dashboard while keeping the site configuration

This clears all the stats you've collected until that point from your dashboard, while keeping the site and its configuration in your account, so the stats start from scratch. Resetting isn't a permanent deletion of your site's data. To permanently delete a site's stats, use Delete site instead, which removes both the stats and the site settings.

Stats for a single page, a single goal or specific custom property values can't be deleted on their own once they've been recorded. If you want to keep test conversions out of a new goal, see how to test a goal.

question: Why do I see (none) all over my custom properties report even though I didn't filter by anything?
reference_answer: When you view the Properties tab without any custom event filter, it returns all the events in your dashboard, including regular pageviews, and many of those don't have the property attached. That's why you see `(none)`. It also appears when a property is sent with no value, as null or undefined, or with some events but not others.
key_facts: (none) appears when a property wasn't sent with every event
Without a custom event filter the tab includes all pageviews
Null or undefined values also show as (none)
answer: When you view the Properties tab without applying a custom event filter, it displays all events in your dashboard, including regular pageviews [1]. Many of these events may not have a custom property attached, which results in the (none) value appearing [1].

citations.quote: However, if you're viewing the **Properties** tab without any custom event filter, it returns all the events in your dashboard (including all regular pageviews) and many of these events may not have a property attached. This is why you see the `(none)` value.

evidence.title: Custom properties
evidence.text:
Plausible will display `(none)` in your dashboard when you send a custom property key with no value, or `null`/`undefined` as a value. Also, when you send one event with a property (e.g. `author`) and another event with the same name, but without the `author` property, then you will also see the `(none)` value because the property has not been sent with every event.

When you filter your dashboard by a particular custom event and look at the **Properties** tab, you should only see `(none)` if some of those events were sent without the property. However, if you're viewing the **Properties** tab without any custom event filter, it returns all the events in your dashboard (including all regular pageviews) and many of these events may not have a property attached. This is why you see the `(none)` value.

question: My site search shows results without changing the URL, so I can't see what people search for. How can I track it?
reference_answer: Send a custom event from your search code whenever a search is made, for example `plausible("Site Search", { props: { search_term: term } })`, and add `Site Search` as a custom event goal in your site settings. Custom events count towards your billable pageviews.
key_facts: Send a Site Search custom event with a search_term prop from your search code
Add Site Search as a custom event goal
Custom events count towards billable pageviews
answer:
If your search box shows results without loading a new page, you can track searches by sending a custom event from your search code [1]. Use the following code, replacing `term` with the variable that holds the visitor's input:

```javascript
plausible("Site Search", { props: { search_term: term } })
```

After adding this, you must add `Site Search` as a custom event goal in your site settings [1]. Please note that these custom events count towards your billable pageviews [1].

Replace `term` with the variable that holds what the visitor typed. Then add `Site Search` as a custom event goal in your site settings. Custom events count towards your billable pageviews.

evidence.text:

```javascript

```

Replace `term` with the variable that holds what the visitor typed. Then add `Site Search` as a custom event goal in your site settings. Custom events count towards your billable pageviews.

evidence.title: Invite team members or external guests and assign roles
evidence.text:
When managing team members, you can choose between five different roles:

1. **Owner** can manage the team, sites, their own API keys, 2FA enforcement, SSO and the subscription. An owner can also delete the team
2. **Admin** can manage team members, sites and their own API keys
3. **Editor** can view all stats dashboards, change site settings and manage their own API keys
4. **Billing** can manage the subscription, payments, invoices and their own API keys
5. **Viewer** can view the stats dashboards of sites that the team owns but cannot create API keys

You can change the role of a team member at any time:

* In the top right menu, click on your account name, make sure you have chosen the team you'd like to manage and then click on the **Team settings**
* You can adjust roles of existing members within the **General** option of the **Team settings**
* Click on the current role next to the name of the person you'd like to change the role for
* Choose a new role for the user

That's it. The team member now has a different role.

You need to be an owner or an admin of a team to change team member roles. Only owners can grant the **Owner** role or change another owner's role. Admins cannot promote themselves or other members to Owner.

question: how can i see how many orders were placed on my squarespace store in plausible? every order has a different url
reference_answer: Completed orders redirect to URLs like /commerce/orders/<id>, so create a pageview goal that groups them with an asterisk: /commerce/orders/*.
key_facts: Order pages follow /commerce/orders/<id>
Create a pageview goal with a wildcard
Use /commerce/orders/*
answer: To track completed orders on your Squarespace site, you can set up a pageview goal [1]. Since each order has a unique URL, you can use an asterisk (*) to group these dynamic pages [1]. For example, you can set up a pageview goal for `/commerce/orders/*` to group all order completion pages [1]. To do this, go to your website's settings in Plausible Analytics, visit the Goals section, and click the + Add goal button [2]. Select Pageview as the trigger and enter the pathname [2].

citations.quote: To track completed orders, you can set up a pageview goal. Since the ID (in our example `/977f8aa0-f618-47d0-8787-ee37b1457cc0`) changes with every order, you will need to group those dynamic pages. You can use asterisks (*) to do so.
For the example above, you can set up a pageview goal `/commerce/orders/*` to group all of the dynamically created order completion pages.

To get started with **Pageview Goals**, go to your website's settings in Plausible Analytics and visit the **Goals** section. You should see an empty list with a prompt to add a goal. Click the **+ Add goal** button to go to the goal creation form. Select `Pageview` as the goal trigger and enter the pathname of the page you would like your visitors to hit, or select the same from the dropdown.

evidence.title: Adding Plausible to Squarespace
evidence.text:
In Squarespace, all completed orders are being redirected to a page with the following format:

`https://yourwebsite.com/commerce/orders/977f8aa0-f618-47d0-8787-ee37b1457cc0`

To track completed orders, you can set up a pageview goal. Since the ID (in our example `/977f8aa0-f618-47d0-8787-ee37b1457cc0`) changes with every order, you will need to group those dynamic pages. You can use asterisks (*) to do so. Asterisks can be placed on either end or in the middle of any page path URL. For the example above, you can set up a pageview goal `/commerce/orders/*` to group all of the dynamically created order completion pages.

evidence.title: Pageview goals
evidence.text:
Pageview goals allow you to measure how many people visit a specific section of your site (for instance dynamically created checkout pages for ecommerce) and get referral sources and other details for those conversions.

Since pageviews are collected automatically, you don’t need to change your website’s code to measure pageview goals. This makes pageview goals the easiest way to start tracking any type of conversion on your site.

Do you run a store and want to track purchases? Do you have a contact form and want to track form submissions? Use pageview goals to track the "thank you" page or the order confirmation page.

To get started with **Pageview Goals**, go to your website's settings in Plausible Analytics and visit the **Goals** section. You should see an empty list with a prompt to add a goal.

Click the **+ Add goal** button to go to the goal creation form.

Select `Pageview` as the goal trigger and enter the pathname of the page you would like your visitors to hit, or select the same from the dropdown. The pathname must match the page path you can see in your Plausible Analytics dashboard.

Next, you'll see the Display Name field, pre-filled based on the pathname. You can optionally edit it now or at any time later.

Add your pageview goal

### Narrow goals with custom properties

When creating a pageview goal, you can optionally narrow it down using custom properties. This lets you turn a broad goal into a more specific one by matching only events with certain property values. For example, you can create a pageview goal for `/dashboard` that only counts visits where `account_type = trial`, letting you measure dashboard engagement specifically from trial users.

Then click the **Add goal** button and you’ll be taken back to the goals page. When you navigate back to your Plausible Analytics dashboard, you should see the number of visitors who reached the specified page or group of pages. Goals are listed at the bottom of your dashboard.
